title: Cold Boot
subject: technology
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: From rewired panels to the first packets, by way of a language nobody expected to outlive us.

entries.clue: 1947 invention that put the vacuum tube out of work
Ada whose notes on the Analytical Engine ran to more than the paper she annotated
Network whose first host-to-host message crashed halfway
entries.explanation: In October 1969 the first message from UCLA to Stanford stopped after two letters.

entries.clue: Innermost layer of an operating system
Disk that kept its name long after it stopped bending

Machine unveiled in 1946 and programmed by moving cables

factCards.text: Ada Lovelace's 1843 notes on Menabrea's paper about the Analytical Engine are roughly three times the length of the paper itself.
factCards.sourceTitle: Science Museum Group — Ada Lovelace collection notes

factCards.text: The first ARPANET message was sent from UCLA to the Stanford Research Institute on 29 October 1969; the system crashed after the first two characters.
factCards.sourceTitle: UCLA Samueli School of Engineering — Internet history archive

factCards.text: The transistor was demonstrated at Bell Labs in December 1947 by Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley, who shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for it.
factCards.sourceTitle: NobelPrize.org — The Nobel Prize in Physics 1956
